title: Define cohort-level statistical power and staged rollback contracts for Optimize evals
creator: Ava Mitchell
description:
Background: Optimize must gate model/quantization/parameter changes with clear, measurable contracts so we can safely roll forward new configurations and rollback quickly when regressions occur. Current practice relies on coarse global thresholds and ad-hoc manual checks. This ticket defines formal statistical power targets and cohort-specific rollback contracts, plus the decisioning surface for staged rollouts and automated alerts.

Problem: Without cohort-aware MDEs and defined stop rules, small regressions in important user segments (e.g., high-value cohorts, low-latency interactive flows) can go unnoticed during canaries and cause customer harm on ramp.

Goal: Produce a spec that: 1) defines minimum detectable effect (MDE) and power targets per cohort and per metric; 2) codifies A/B decision rules (frequentist and optional Bayesian fallback) including multiple-comparison corrections; 3) specifies staged rollout percentages, cooldown windows, and automatic rollback triggers tied to composite signals; 4) integrates with Console dashboards, Optimize eval harness, and runbooks so on-call can execute rollbacks rapidly.
scope: Define cohort taxonomy for Optimize (traffic, product flow, customer tier, prompt complexity).
Specify per-cohort MDE, alpha, beta, and sample-size guidance for primary and secondary metrics.
Formalize A/B decision rules and sequential monitoring (SPRT / alpha-spending / group-sequential), with safe early-stop rules.
Design staged rollout schedule and automatic rollback thresholds tied to composite signals and severity tiers.
Define required dashboard charts, alerting rules, and links to the rollback playbook in Console.
Author acceptance criteria and handoff docs for Eng/Analytics/Console teams to implement.
Compatibility: work applies to Optimize evals for generation, chat, and embeddings flows.
out_of_scope: Rewriting the entire Optimize evaluation engine (this ticket only defines contracts and requirements).
Implementing model-side changes or kernel optimizations — engineering tasks will be separate issues.
Full safety review of model outputs; safety signals are included as metrics but deep-moderation policy updates are out of scope.
acceptance_criteria: A formal spec document exists and is reviewed by PM, Analytics, RS/Applied ML, and Console owners.
Per-cohort MDE table with sample-size formulas and example calculations for small/medium/large cohorts.
A/B decision rules defined for both fixed-horizon and sequential monitoring; includes multiple-test correction approach.
Concrete staged rollout recipe: percentage steps, wait durations, minimum event counts per step, and automatic-block criteria.
Rollback triggers enumerated into at least three severity classes (info, degrade, emergency) with specific metric thresholds and CI/p-value rules.
Monitoring and alerting requirements documented with example Grafana/Console queries and expected alert destinations (pager/email/team-channel).
A short runbook that maps alert to exact rollback steps (manual and automated) with links to the Console action buttons and GitHub rollout PRs.
statistical_spec: Primary testing approach: frequentist A/B with sequential monitoring. Default alpha=0.01 for high-impact cohorts, alpha=0.05 for others; power (1-beta)=0.8 target for primary metrics. MDEs expressed in relative change for each metric and cohort (examples provided). Multiple comparisons: hierarchical testing where primary metric per cohort is tested first; secondary metrics use Benjamini-Hochberg FDR with q=0.05. For long-running canaries, use an alpha-spending function (O'Brien-Fleming style) or Group Sequential with pre-specified looks. We will allow a Bayesian posterior-check mode for low-volume cohorts where frequentist methods lack power; the spec includes priors and posterior probability thresholds (e.g., P(delta < 0) > 0.95 for degradation).
sampling_strategy: Stratify prompt sampling by: customer tier (free/pro), latency-sensitive vs batch, prompt length bucket, and safety-risk flag. For A/B traffic allocation: use randomized assignment at request-time with deterministic hashing to avoid cross-contamination. Minimum sample counts: small cohort = 1,000 sessions or 10,000 requests (whichever triggers earlier conservative action), medium = 10k sessions, large = 100k sessions. Rare cohorts: aggregate across multiple time windows with adjusted MDEs or apply Bayesian pooling across similar cohorts. Ensure promptset test harness can seed stratified prompt lists and record cohort tags in evaluation telemetry.
rollback_triggers: Emergency: Any cohort-specific absolute increase in safety-critical flags (hallucination label, toxicity) exceeding 0.5% absolute and statistically significant at alpha=0.01 triggers immediate rollback and incident page (pager on-call).

Degrade: Primary quality metric drop > MDE for cohort and 95% CI not overlapping zero triggers pause of further rollout and investigator notification. If confirmed, rollback to previous stable variant.
Cost/Latency: Token-cost per response increase > 20% or p95 latency increase > 2x baseline with significance triggers staged rollback and throttled traffic diversion to fallback model variant.
Composite: If at least two secondary signals (safety flags, quality, error rate) exceed soft thresholds within a 24h window, trigger an automated canary pause and secondary manual review.

Sequential alarms: If monitoring shows sustained negative trend across three consecutive monitoring windows (per alpha-spending plan), trigger escalation even if single-window thresholds are not exceeded.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (Canary): 0.5% traffic for 24-72 hours with dedicated cohort-level metrics and required minimum event counts. Proceed only if no emergency triggers and primary metric within acceptance band.
Phase 1: 5% traffic for at least 48 hours and until sample-size conditions met per cohort. Monitor for degrade triggers and run sequential tests at predefined looks.
Phase 2: 25% traffic for 48-72 hours, require cross-cohort stability and no critical alerts.
Phase 3: 100% ramp with a final cool-down window (24h) where automated throttles may reduce traffic if conditioned alerts appear.
Rollback mechanism: automated rollback when emergency triggers fire; manual rollback options for degrade triggers per runbook with pre-approved rollback owners listed in Console.
monitoring_signals: Primary quality metric (cohort-specific relevance score or task-specific accuracy proxy).
Safety flags rate (moderation / hallucination detectors), broken out by severity.
User-visible latency (p50/p95) and error rate (5xx / timeouts).
Token cost per response (normalized by prompt length) and cost-per-1000-requests for billing-sensitive customers.
Eng reliability signals: inference failures, model OOMs, infra retries.
observability_requirements: Per-cohort dashboard tile showing primary metric, CI bands, sample sizes, and trendline annotated with rollout phase.
Alerting rules with destinations mapped: emergency -> pager and workspace incident channel; degrade -> email + product slack channel; info -> metric dashboard notifications.
Retention: evaluation telemetry retained for 90 days with aggregated weekly rollups for longer-term drift analysis.
Correlation: ability to slice alerts by model variant, quantization level, region, and customer tier in Console.
notes: Tradeoffs: tighter alpha reduces false positives but increases risk of missing regressions; cohort MDEs should reflect product-level risk appetite (higher for high-value cohorts).
Open question: default MDEs for conversational NLU metrics — need RS input to translate metric deltas into user-perceived regression.
Implementation dependency: requires Console feature to attach cohort tags to live traffic and to display per-cohort CI bands; ENG ticket(s) must prioritize those dashboards.
We should run a simulation using historical telemetry to validate the MDE table and sample-size guidance before final sign-off.
